avenues.name: The achievement ledger
avenues.thesis: A 298-row, event-anchored, per-row-verified corpus of US and Chinese achievements 1926–2026; 294 rows ESTABLISHED under a published promotion standard. The full 1926–2025 chronological corpus is processed, plus author-proposed per-row passes (batch 11: physical-manufacturing and 2023–2025 achievements; batch 12: maritime and defense-industrial; batch 13: the national-security view; batch 14: two US venture-capital / small-business-R&D rows anchoring Figure Va; batch 15: two China rows — 'Big Fund III' state chip capital and the open-weight Kimi K3, for Figure Vb's state-capital and frontier-AI layers) adding rows on both sides — each through the same ritual. Rows also carry a country-blind natsec / dual-use tag (Amendment 5) driving Figure III.

avenues.name: Coverage shape
avenues.thesis: Facts about the corpus under the published selection rule: US coverage is steady and invention/deployment-heavy; China's is thin early, rises late, and is completion/milestone-heavy. A statement about the ledger — NOT a momentum verdict about the world.

avenues.name: The momentum index
avenues.thesis: Now computed and shown as a constructed index (Option C gate: ESTABLISHED rows only, non-ESTABLISHED rows excluded and named). Primary = baseline equal weighting; bands span four published weightings; whiskers show the excluded non-ESTABLISHED rows (1946–1955 and 2016–2025). Re-weightable, rubric published — true only within its scope, never a measured verdict.

avenues.name: Early-century China floor
avenues.thesis: 1926–1945 China coverage is a floor, not a fact — real historical thinness compounded by English-language source bias. Posted as an open challenge: readers who know this literature can raise it, for named credit.

avenues.name: Verification in progress
avenues.thesis: Live status: 294 ESTABLISHED, 1 OPEN-UNVERIFIED, 3 REPORTED. Batches 1–10 processed the full 1926–2025 corpus; a straggler sweep resolved leftovers; batch 11 added twelve ESTABLISHED physical-manufacturing/2023–2025 rows plus one REPORTED (a Chinese EUV-lithography claim, interested-party sourced — confirmed progress is DUV not EUV); batch 12 added two ESTABLISHED China maritime rows (shipbuilding dominance; PLA Navy largest by hull count, with the mandatory US-leads-by-tonnage caveat); batch 13 added USS Gerald R. Ford and eight further defense rows (four US, four China) plus one REPORTED (the 2021 hypersonic test — independent FT report recorded alongside China's spacecraft denial), and a country-blind natsec/dual-use tag across the corpus (Figure III); batch 14 added two US rows — American Research and Development (1946, the first modern venture-capital firm) and the SBIR program (1982) — so every founder-regime tick in Figure Va now anchors to a ledger row; batch 15 added two China rows for Figure Vb — 'Big Fund III' (2024, ¥344bn/~$47.5bn registered capital, the largest state chip fund; SAMR-registered, Bloomberg/Reuters-corroborated) and Moonshot AI's open-weight Kimi K3 (July 2026, filed narrowly on independent LMArena/Artificial Analysis benchmarks and explicitly recorded as trailing the leading US closed models). Announced or not-yet-operational items (DF-17 parade reveal, US hypersonic weapons, Linglong-One SMR, second-gen batteries, the ¥1T 2025 national VC guidance fund — a target with no disclosed paid-in capital, Chinese-origin sourcing, held as Figure Vb annotation only, Columbia-class SSBN, AUKUS transfers) were held, not filed. Just ONE row stays open: the Chengdu–Chongqing Railway (CN-1952-1). The 2026 window is also not yet closed.

avenues.name: What we make of it
avenues.thesis: Interpretation, NOT record (OPEN-CAVEATED): six reader-facing claims, each citing its own rows or figures, offered to be re-weighted and disagreed with. (i) The century bifurcated by DOMAIN, not by winner — the US holds the frontier of bits/bio/space, China won the physical economy. (ii) Two systems optimized for different things — private-capital frontier conversion vs state-priority deployment tempo. (iii) The founder's answer is conditional — the US for most founders and sectors by regime continuity, capital depth and openness; the exception is nationally-aligned hard tech under state capital, abundant if aligned and closed if not. (iv) The open experiment — whether nationalized venture capital sustains FRONTIER innovation over a decade is unresolved, hence a forecast, not a finding. (v) A falsification menu of what would change our minds. (vi) Leverage is mutual and domain-split — China's chokepoints are atoms (rare-earth, batteries, manufacturing), the US's are bits and tools (export controls, EUV, compute, listing venues); both spend to escape the other's grip and the spending is the proof, with atoms-leverage eroding slower than bits (an OPEN-CAVEATED direction, not a fact). Supersedes the walled synthesis_frame candidate note (kept as provenance).

avenues.name: Forecast F1 — the physical economy (authorial bet)
avenues.thesis: AUTHORIAL BET (labeled as such): by end-2030 China holds a MAJORITY of global annual industrial-robot installations (IFR World Robotics series) AND at least three major Chinese automakers operate highly-automated, dark-capable production lines that are independently documented. Falsification: refuted if China is below 50% of annual industrial-robot installations at the 2029 checkpoint, or fewer than three dark-capable Chinese automaker lines are independently documented by end-2030. Revisit dates logged in verification_log.md.

avenues.name: Forecast F2 — the open experiment (dossier, neutral)
avenues.thesis: DOSSIER FORECAST, direction deliberately NEUTRAL — this is the experiment, not a rooting interest: by end-2030 state-guided capital produces at least one independently-verified FRONTIER outcome — domestic EUV-class lithography in production use, OR a Chinese frontier model LEADING independent benchmarks (not fast-following) sustained at least six months, OR at least three commercially-operating SMR units. Tracking hooks: the standing EUV REPORTED row (CN-2025-3) and the Linglong-One SMR revisit. Falsification: refuted if NONE of the three occurs by end-2030 — stated as the single strongest datapoint against the nationalized-LP (state-as-venture-capitalist) model.

avenues.name: Forecast F3 — the venture-capital verdict
avenues.thesis: DOSSIER FORECAST: through 2030 Chinese private venture capital stays BELOW half its 2021 real peak (PitchBook-class series) AND the US remains the primary venue for non-Chinese high-tech founders. Falsification: a sustained recovery of Chinese private VC past 50% of the 2021 peak refutes it — and, if refuted, the Figure Vb judgment box is rewritten (said here so the bet has teeth). Revisit dates logged in verification_log.md.
avenues.signpost: through 2030 · annual PitchBook-class VC series checks

checks._comment: Single source of truth for the consistency-check RULES. Both index.html's console and verification/verify_numbers.py read these, so a threshold can never drift between the page and the verifier. Change a rule HERE and both sides enforce it on next run. (The check LOGIC is still written in each language — see AUTHORING.md — but the rules it enforces live only here.)
